signal_status.original_signal: Iran war and Strait of Hormuz
signal_status.headline: Operation Epic Fury ongoing: US-Israel strikes on Iran nuclear and leadership targets; Strait of Hormuz shipping status under active monitoring
signal_status.summary: Operation Epic Fury, the joint US-Israel military campaign targeting Iranian nuclear infrastructure, missile programs, and senior leadership, killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and triggered a succession crisis within Iran's Assembly of Experts. The Strait of Hormuz — through which approximately 20% of global oil supply transits — faces elevated disruption risk from Iranian naval and mine-laying capabilities as a retaliatory pressure tool. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy has historically used asymmetric Hormuz operations during periods of maximum leadership stress, making current conditions a heightened chokepoint risk environment.
signal_status.enrichment_note: Draws on training knowledge of Operation Epic Fury, Khamenei's death, Hormuz transit volumes, and IRGC asymmetric naval doctrine through early 2026.

signal_status.headline: Schedule Policy Career reclassification of ~50,000 federal positions to at-will employment took effect March 2026 amid active union litigation

signal_status.original_signal: Arkansas state-level preemption and datacenter leverage
signal_status.headline: Arkansas preemption-utility-datacenter nexus advances structurally without headline coverage, compounding democratic accountability erosion
signal_status.summary: The Arkansas model combines three reinforcing mechanisms: judicial preemption of ballot initiatives (Good Day Farm ruling), legislative utility rate capture favoring large industrial consumers (Acts 373/548), and federal energy bypass proposals (DATA Act/CREU designation) that would remove state regulatory authority over AI datacenter power consumption. With $17B+ in committed datacenter capital from Google, AVAIO, and others, and L3Harris's Camden facility anchoring defense-industrial convergence, Arkansas represents a fully integrated template for state-level structural leverage that operates below the visibility threshold of national media cycles. Governor Huckabee Sanders and Senator Tom Cotton provide the political durability that makes this model exportable to other states.
signal_status.enrichment_note: Draws on training knowledge of Arkansas Supreme Court preemption jurisprudence, Acts 373/548, datacenter capital commitments, DATA Act proposals, and L3Harris Camden facility through early 2026.
